paper_title: Optical Design of Transparent Thin Metal Electrodes to Enhance In-Coupling and Trapping of Light in Flexible Polymer Solar Cells
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Advanced Materials - 2012 - Salinas - Optical Design of Transparent Thin Metal Electrodes to Enhance In‐Coupling and/auto/Advanced Materials - 2012 - Salinas - Optical Design of Transparent Thin Metal Electrodes to Enhance In‐Coupling and.md

knowledge_points.content: Tellurium dioxide (TeO2) serves as an effective seed layer for silver (Ag) ultrathin metal films (UTMF) because it has a low wetting angle (~50°) and high refractive index (η ~ 2.15).
knowledge_points.evidence: The wetting angles of molten silver over substrates treated with TeO2 and MoO3 (~50°) have been reported to be much lower than that using other metal oxides... TeO2 and MoO3 not only are transparent to visible light but also have quite low melting points... allowing them to be easily evaporated.

knowledge_points.content: The hybrid TeO2/Ag (12 nm) electrode achieves a sheet resistance of 7.02 Ω □⁻¹, which is significantly lower than the 13.53 Ω □⁻¹ measured for a standard ITO electrode.
knowledge_points.evidence: Fortunately, high transparency and low sheet resistance (Rsheet-TeO2 = 7.02 Ω □⁻¹ compared to 13.53 Ω □⁻¹ for ITO) can be achieved when high refractive index TeO2 is used in combination with 12 nm thick Ag.

knowledge_points.content: Polymer solar cells using TeO2(40 nm)/Ag(12 nm) electrodes reached power conversion efficiencies (PCE) of 6.6% on glass and 5.8% on flexible PEN substrates, surpassing their ITO-based counterparts (6.5% and 5.6% respectively).
knowledge_points.evidence: The PCE of the devices using TeO2 (40 nm)/Ag substrates (PCEglass-Ag = 6.6% PCEPEN-Ag = 5.8%) surpasses those observed on ITO (PCEglass-ITO = 6.5%, PCEPEN-ITO = 5.6%).

knowledge_points.content: The use of a higher refractive index material like TeO2 (η ~ 2.15) as an optical coupling layer enables higher anticipated short-circuit currents (Jsc-100%) compared to lower refractive index materials like MoO3 (η ~ 1.75).
knowledge_points.evidence: However, the higher refractive index TeO2 allows the system to reach higher Jsc-100% (when a 40 nm thick TeO2 film is used) than that calculated for ITO.

knowledge_points.content: A microcavity resonance is established between the 12 nm thick Ag transparent electrode and the 120 nm thick Ag back electrode, which amplifies the internal electric field and compensates for the lower transparency of the UTMF compared to ITO.
knowledge_points.evidence: Although the transparency of the hybrid TeO2/Ag electrode is lower than ITO, the resulting microcavity resonant condition amplifies the electric field within the cell to give higher performance than the ITO based devices.

knowledge_points.content: To prevent the acidic aqueous PEDOT:PSS solution from etching the thin Ag electrode, a buffer layer consisting of a PEDOT:PSS/IPA/butanol mixture (1:2:2 ratio) is applied prior to the standard PEDOT:PSS deposition.
knowledge_points.evidence: To avoid possible etching of Ag by the aqueous solution of PEDOT:PSS, a layer of PEDOT:PSS/IPA/butanol in proportion of 1/2/2 was applied first over the Ag substrate and then the aqueous solution of PEDOT:PSS was spin-coated.

knowledge_points.content: The Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) is used to calculate the ideal current density (Jsc-100%) by integrating the exciton generation rate across the active layer, assuming an internal quantum efficiency (IQE) of 100%.
knowledge_points.evidence: Assuming IQE is 100%, the rates of exciton generation and charge generation will be the same, therefore, we can estimate an ideal current density with no loses (Jsc-100%) by integrating the generation rate over the whole active layer.

knowledge_points.content: Flexible PSCs with TeO2/Ag electrodes demonstrate superior mechanical stability, maintaining or slightly improving performance (from 5.7% to 5.8% PCE) after 91 bending cycles at a radius of 0.64 cm, whereas ITO-based devices degrade immediately.
knowledge_points.evidence: In contrast, the performance of the devices with TeO2 (40 nm)/Ag (12 nm) electrode are much more stable even after greater than 100 bending cycles. In deed, the performance of the TeO2 based device increased slightly with the bends, growing from an original PCE = 5.7% to 5.8% after 91 bending cycles.

knowledge_points.content: The validity of the optical TMM model is confirmed by the high degree of similarity between the simulated absorption spectra in the active layer and the experimental External Quantum Efficiency (EQE) curves.
knowledge_points.evidence: The extraordinary similarity between measured EQE and modeled absorption curves is a good testimony of the validity of the optical model.

knowledge_points.content: The optimal thickness for the TeO2 layer to maximize light trapping in the Ag-Ag microcavity is approximately 40 nm, which corresponds to roughly a quarter-wavelength (λ/4) optical thickness.
knowledge_points.evidence: By introducing a highly transparent (κ ~ 0), high refractive index (η ~ 2.15) TeO2 film of approximately a quarter wavelength... in resonance with the Ag-Ag microcavity, the total reflection of the UTMF can be dramatically reduced... the election of the thickness of both active layer and TeO2 film that maximizes Jsc-100%... (dTeO2 = 40 nm).
